newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court confirms Commission has no duty to buy ore.
newsitem.headline: Court confirms Commission has no duty to buy ore.

text.p: The European Court of Justice rejected an appeal on Thursday to overturn a Court of First Instance ruling that the European Commission has no duty to purchase ore supplies mined in the Community.

The Commission, along with the Euratom Agency, operates under a purchase approval scheme to ensure future supplies of ore, source materials and special fissile materials remain available for use within the Community at a reasonable cost.

Relations with suppliers worldwide are maintained to promote that diversity of supply, but they do not create a legitimate expectation on the part of suppliers that the Euratom Agency will purchase available ore, the court said.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: Portuguese)

"Appeal - EAEC - Supply - Right of option and exclusive right of the Euratom Supply Agency to conclude contracts for the supply of ores, source materials and sepcial fissile materials - Infringement of the rules of the Treaty - Community preference - Principles of good faith and legitimate expectations - Non-contractual liability"
Empressa Nacional de uranio SA (ENU), appellant
Appeal against Court of First Instance Joined Cases T-458/93 and T-523/93, ENU v Commission (1995) ECR II-2459, seeking to have that judgment set aside
the other party to the proceeding being
THE COURT OF FIRST INSTANCE hereby
2. Orders the appellant to pay the costs.
